author: Trapping Value
title: Colony NorthStar ( CLNS ) was formed in a tumultuous time th
text:
Colony NorthStar ( CLNS ) was formed in a tumultuous time through the merger of three companies: NorthStar Asset Management, NorthStar Real Estate Finance, and Colony Capital. The move was designed to unlock the value of NorthStar Real Estate Finance which was then trading at a substantial discount to its estimated NAV. We watched this one from the sidelines and took an initial plunge (we wish that just meant bought the stock) about 3 months back.
CLNS Total Return Price data by YCharts That has not been pleasant.
As our belief goes, the market always makes the news. This time the decline is creating rumors that the dividend is scheduled to be cut. We examine the dividend coverage and give our thoughts on this REIT as a whole.
Definitely the worst of times Charles Dickens would have started this article with an unequivocal "It was the worst of times." CLNS has underperformed the REIT index by a substantial margin and we could not find another REIT that did as badly over this time frame. W.P. Carey ( WPC ), a diversified REIT that we compared some of CLNS metrics too, has fared substantially better as well.
CLNS Total Return Price data by YCharts Fundamentally, to the best of our knowledge, nothing has changed dramatically enough to justify this kind of selloff. Some might argue that CLNS does have an above-average exposure to the healthcare sector which is vulnerable from fallout effects from the recent changes in the tax code.

Source: CLNS Q3-2017 financials 
But even there it has great diversification with medical office buildings and hospitals acting as more stable revenue sources. With about 56% of revenues in that segment coming from private pay, CLNS really should have less issues than diversified healthcare REITs like Ventas ( VTR ) and Welltower Inc. ( HCN ), both of which it has substantially underperformed. Other segments including industrial and hospitality are doing quite well with a strong economy and extremely strong e-commerce expansion. Fundamentally we found nothing that could justify a selloff of even half this magnitude. 
Dividend Coverage When we first wrote about this, many questioned the dividend coverage. Specifically, the concern was whether CLNS was generating this mainly through asset sales and gains? This stemmed from the supplementary material shown in Q3-2017.

Source: CLNS supplementary information 
The Funds from operations (FFO) appears to be extremely low and is going through multiple adjustments to reach the Core FFO of $193,351. Investors were worried about the $50,884 in gains which are likely not reproducible. 
Before we start with this explanation, we would like to point out that there are some parts of this that are extremely complex and an entire book might prove inadequate. We will however tackle 3 primary questions on the dividend.
1) Is Core FFO being driven by one-time gains?
2) Are all additions and subtractions from FFO valid?
3) What is true dividend coverage and what is it likely to be going forward?
Is Core FFO being driven by one-time gains? No. People who are looking at Q3-2017 are missing what happened to this line the last two quarters. In Both Q1 and Q2, this line was a negative and YTD this line has lowered the starting FFO number.
Q1-2017
Q2-2017
Hence the year to date number is subtracting almost $30 million from the starting FFO number. This calculation is, however, a requirement as CLNS has a segment of "Other equity and debt" where does trade more frequently. This line actually removes the impact of those trades and focuses on the underlying portfolio.
Another way to understand that things did not fall off a cliff in Q3-2017 (and required asset sale gains to help cover dividend) is to look at the 3 month and 9 month segmental NOI.
In each segment the 3 month performance is a bit greater than one-third of the year to date NOI. This is due to CLNS starting its trading on January 10, 2017 (so a shortened Q1-2017), but overall numbers here support that Q3-2017 was at least as good as the rest of the year. 
Are all additions and subtractions from FFO valid? While the format is standard, we are not too pleased with the equity based compensation which is extraordinarily huge. Cash rewards are fine as they are directly counted but the $86.4 million year to date of awards to NSAM executive is way too much. 
While this does inflate the Core FFO as this is an expense, it is also standard practice to do so. The $86.4 million is 15% of the overall core FFO and one can argue that dividend coverage should be calculated taking that into account. 
What is true dividend coverage and what is it likely to be going forward? Core FFO for the 9 months ended September 30, 2017 was $570.05 million. Subtracting out, NSAM equity awards (merger related) leaves us with $483.66 million. With weighted average shares at 531 million, total payout at $0.81 comes to $430.11 million, giving an adjusted payout ratio of 88.9%. CLNS has made asset sales during the year and it will show in Core FFO trending lower and minority interest creeping up. But these funds will be deployed either through buybacks or different asset purchases. Overall we think 2018 coverage will improve from these levels as NSAM compensation drops lower.
Conclusion CLNS has been a difficult stock to own but we reanalyzed the situation and added 2.5X our original investment at $8.98, giving us a weighted average of $9.95 on our shares. The dividend appears to be covered and we like this diversified REIT's multiple. It is a complicated REIT to analyze and that may be the market's major gripe with it along with a compensation structure that leaves a lot of room for improvement. We will be watching for progress on both fronts in 2018. 
On our scale of 1-10, where 1 would be "Avoid like the bubonic plague" and 10 would be "Buy like this is Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) in March 2009," we would rate CLNS a STRONG BUY and at 8.5 .
